speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what specific upgrades are planned for the national grid and energy infrastructure to accommodate new energy sources like small modular reactors and ammonia; (b) what is the projected timeline for implementing these upgrades; and (c) how is the Government ensuring that infrastructure and grid readiness align with the commercial availability of these technologies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: We are, however, closely monitoring developments in SMR technology to assess if and when they can be and may be safe enough and feasible for Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The pilot will help us evaluate the feasibility of scaling up ammonia power generation in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: If ammonia power generation becomes feasible, we will naturally consider building the infrastructure required to support this new pathway.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Just two quick supplementary questions for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: The first is, I note that there will be a Future Energy Fund which will be set up by the year-end.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I just wanted to ask if there is a specific amount that will be ear-marked for these two new technologies for the infrastructure and grid upgrades that will be necessary, should we decide to go ahead with implementing this on a larger scale.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Second, I note the Minister's response that the Government is still monitoring SMR technology.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: At the same time, I also saw a recent piece of news that the EMA Chief Executive shared that SMR technology is actually a possible solution to power Singapore's data centres.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, on that note, I just wanted to ask if there is a certain timeline on this.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: Given that the last time we did a feasibility study was about 10 years ago, are there any plans to then conduct a proper study to see whether it is possible to power, not just the data centre industry, but that of our energy requirements?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But with time, we will come back and lay out what are the amounts that we have been setting aside to develop and to invest in, to seed and to catalyse some of the developments.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, the first point is, perhaps for the Member's own understanding, the first focus will be on the interconnectors and this is relating to the renewable energy imports.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the SMRs today, while there have been a lot of discussions, there has been also a lot of publicity around the potential for SMRs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, that being said, it still holds quite a fair bit of promise because the safety buffer zones are significantly less than during the time when we did the first feasibility study.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think that was back in around 2012, where the safety buffer zones for the conventional large-sized nuclear reactors did not make it possible or feasible for us to be considering investing in such type of technology within our island state.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, today, given the nascency of some of these projects, we have not decided whether we will move on to another feasibility study.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Our main focus is on understanding the safety, the reliability and the technical aspects of SMR type of technology.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think in the context of thinking forward, what are some possible pathways we can use – because we have committed to a net zero target by 2050, so what are some of the alternative pathways we can do for us to continue to fulfil our zero emission target and at the same time accommodate high-growth industries, whether it is in semiconductors or even wafer fabs or even data centres?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We will explore all possible pathways in order for us to enable our policy space to be able to accommodate some of these set-ups.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I have also shared in this House that we are also looking at geothermal exploration.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: As I have earlier on shared, we are considering using ammonia as a pathfinder.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are also looking at the possibility of carbon capture and storage.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We are also working with like-minded countries for implementation agreements according to Article 6 of the Paris Accords on carbon credits as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, it is one of multiple pathways that EMA and the Energy Division of the Ministry of Trade and Industry have embarked on to explore every possible means we can to decarbonise and within our confines of policy space, in terms of affordability and sustainability.
